title: Choose Siteline's visual world
question: The roll assigned the METRO system map. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: System Map
options.lineage: Houston METRO rail and bus system maps: route colors, ringed stations, transfer points
options.thesis: The agent's run is a transit line: plan steps are stations, parallel data scouts branch off and rejoin at the approval transfer, and the ranked sites are the line's final stops.
materials: flat route colors on white map paper
options.viewport: Left rail: the run drawn as a vertical route line, stations lighting up as the agent works, scout branches splitting off in their own colors. Center: the Houston hex map, fit shaded in one route color. Bottom: ranked sites as numbered terminus stops with customers won set large.
options.risk: If the route line is decoration rather than the live run state, it becomes a costume; it must be the actual progress view.

raised.raise: Rank numerals become the only display type: every site is a numbered stop, and the number is the headline.
One action color, reserved for what can be pressed (approve, run, open tour); route colors never mark buttons.
Site markers on the map scale with customers won, so the map ranks before you read the list.
Result columns never move between runs; only their values change, so the demo and daily use read the same.

options.label: Leasing Flyer
options.lineage: commercial broker leasing flyers and offering memoranda: aerial with the site outlined, demographic ring tables
options.thesis: Each recommended site is presented the way brokers already present space, with Siteline's verified numbers in place of the broker's pitch.
materials: yellow site outline over a muted base map
options.viewport: Map with the chosen site outlined in broker yellow and its catchment rings; right column a flyer-style sheet: address, AVAILABLE badge, size and rent, a ring table of customers won.
options.risk: Familiar: it looks like CoStar and LoopNet, which is also where most runs in this category land; the agent's reasoning gets less stage.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.case: Ranked sites fit departure rows, but owners don't identify with a terminal board and the map loses the stage.
options.kept: Fixed columns: rows re-rank, columns never move.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.case: Magnitude dots suit ranked sites, but a night sky reads as astronomy, not Houston real estate.
options.kept: Dot size carries rank on the map.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.case: Friendly, but thumb-first cards bury the map and the agent's work; weak for a projector.
options.kept: One action color reserved for actions.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.case: Coded labels hide meaning; owners need plain words and judges need to read it instantly.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.case: Rich system, but a reference manual frames Siteline as documentation, not a decision tool.

options.label: Zoo Guide Map
options.lineage: illustrated garden and zoo guide maps
options.case: Playful lobes fight the hex grid and read as leisure, not leasing.

canonCard.label: GIS dashboard, done well
canonCard.thesis: The site-selection category standard: dark sidebar, full map, filter chips and result cards, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Dark left panel with steps and factors, full map, a results drawer of cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Placer.ai, Esri and every site-selection dashboard by design.
